newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian minister feuds with boss of state paper.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian minister feuds with boss of state paper.

text.p: A war of words between Nigeria's information minister and the boss of the majority state-owned Daily Times, black Africa's largest newspaper, erupted in the local press on Thursday.

A statement from Daily Times sole administrator, Peter Enahoro, published in most Nigerian newspapers said remarks made by Information Minister Walter Ofonagoro could damage his efforts to rebuild the more than 70-year-old daily paper.

"Circulation figures are going up, advertisement levels are rising...one can only pray that these developments are not sabotaged by the honourable minister's remarks," said Enahoro, a respected journalist and satirist.

Ofonagoro, in remarks published in the local press on Tuesday, described the Daily Times as "sick" and heavily in debt. He said the government would do nothing to bail out the newspaper which he said was antagonistic.

"The honourable minister does not substantiate his claims of antagonism with any evidence except, perhaps, he regards his complaint that his photograph is now used sparingly on the front page," Enahoro said.

Enahoro said since he took over the Daily Times last year the company had refused to pay for air tickets and accommodation requested by the minister and stopped the practice of allowing ministry officials to place personal advertisements for free.

Enahoro, who edited the Daily Times at the age of 24 in the 1960s, is the brother of Anthony Enahoro, the exiled leader of the NADECO group which opposes the rule of military ruler General Sani Abacha.
